NO. 020 · Songbirds & City Birds / Estrildidae · Munias

Scaly-breasted Munia

斑文鸟 · bān wén niǎo Lonchura punctulata
Resident Common 11–12 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The little bird with fish scales on its belly

Dark scale-like markings cover the breast and belly like a suit of armour. Scaly-breasted Munias move in parties of a dozen, rising and falling over seeding grass, then drop in head-first so that only a row of small heads shows.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • UnderpartsThroat chestnut; breast and belly white with dark edges to each feather, giving crisp scaling — the most reliable mark.
  • UpperpartsHead, neck and back chestnut-brown with paler fringes, finely scaled overall.
  • BillThick, conical and grey-blue, built for cracking grass seed and grain.
  • TailShort and wedge-shaped, the central feathers longer and pointed.

Behaviour

A seed-eater first: grass seed and grain, with a little insect food. Highly gregarious in parties of ten to several dozen, with a bounding flight and constant calling. The nest is a large ball woven from grass in a bush or tree. Resident here, commonest at the edges of paddies and grassland.

Voice

A soft 'kitty-kitty' or 'peet-peet', quiet individually but noticeable when the flock calls together, and continuous in flight.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen rice paddies
  • Jinwan grassy slopes
  • Hengqin wetland fringes
  • park lawns
Field note
Versus White-rumped Munia: Scaly-breasted has the scaly underparts and a grey-blue bill; White-rumped is plain brown with a white rump and a heavier grey-black bill. The two often flock together.
